display: Indie game dev in Berlin making a pixel-art fishing game (Slow Water) in Godot; happy to talk tools, art pipeline and playtests.

signals.text: I'm working toward a Slow Water demo for the February Next Fest and could use all the practical help I can get.
I keep polishing the water shader instead of finishing the quest scripting. I'd like an accountability buddy who will ask me 'did you ship the boring thing today?'
I need music and sound effects. I compose badly, and about half the game's audio is still missing.
In our last playtest, everyone fished for the rare carp for an hour and nobody finished the tutorial. I want outside eyes on my onboarding.
I'm learning German properly (B1) and want people to practise with, ideally patient ones who let me make mistakes.
A few people on Discord asked for my sprite-sheet-to-journal Godot plugin. I haven't cleaned it up and might do it in November.
My grant milestone report is due Nov 15 and I have to explain why milestone three slipped without it sounding like excuses.
The second half of the lake, the weather system and save-file migration are still unbuilt, so scope is my main schedule risk.
My money is tight until the grant's third tranche, so paid work or small commissions that don't involve crunch would help.

My residence permit expires Dec 14 and the Ausländerbehörde appointment has slipped three times to Oct 29. I'm looking for someone who really understands freelancer permit extensions and the Fiktionsbescheinigung in Berlin.
A publisher showcase in January interests me, but I can't plan that far ahead while my residence status is uncertain.
I'm quietly worried the game won't sell enough to justify two years of work, and I'm carrying a lot of bureaucratic stress mostly alone.

offers.text: Six years of Godot 4 and C++ engine tooling. I can help debug gameplay code, frame-rate-dependent bugs, and editor plugins.
A full Aseprite pixel-art pipeline (about 900 finished sprites). I can talk through workflow, animation, and palette discipline.
I built a 24-colour palette hand-picked from a lake photo. I can share how I chose it and plan to write a palette post after the demo.
I have a playable 40-minute vertical slice. I can swap playtests with other indie devs and give structured feedback.
I ran a Steam page to 3,100 wishlists. I can share what I did with the page, capsule art and early marketing.
I know how to apply for and report on a small regional media-fund grant as an independent developer in Germany.
I'm a native American English speaker, so I can offer English conversation or proofreading in exchange for German practice.
I have a Godot plugin that turns a sprite sheet into a flip-through journal UI. I could clean it up and release it.
I have a desk in a shared Neukölln studio with other game devs, and I can introduce visitors there.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a composer or sound designer who loves cozy, slow games. I'd like to score a small pixel-art game for a credit and a modest fee.
catchers.can: Jonas can talk through Slow Water's audio needs, share the tone and reference tracks, and agree a small scoped piece of work that avoids crunch.
catchers.confirm: Are you comfortable with a calm, ambient game and with working to a small fixed scope rather than open-ended revisions?

catchers.hypo: I run a small Godot meetup and need someone to talk about shipping a first commercial game solo. Can you speak or share slides?
catchers.can: Jonas can give a short, honest talk or write-up on a solo workflow, the Steam page, and pixel-art production.
catchers.confirm: Is the event in Berlin or online, and not requiring travel outside the Schengen area?

catchers.hypo: I'm an indie dev heading to Next Fest in February and looking for people to swap playtests and demo feedback with.
catchers.can: Jonas can run a mutual playtest swap and give notes on tutorials and first-hour retention.
catchers.confirm: Do you have a playable build of at least ten minutes that you can send within a few weeks?

catchers.hypo: I make a tower defence game and need to know which publishers actually pay and communicate. I heard you know someone with publisher experience.
catchers.can: Through his studio neighbour Marek, who makes tower defence games and has had bad luck with publishers, Jonas can set up a two-way introduction to compare notes.
catchers.confirm: Are you a developer with a playable build, not just a pitch deck, and happy to share honest experiences back?

catchers.hypo: I'm learning German as an adult and my teacher is too gentle. Can you recommend a strict teacher who really corrects articles?
catchers.can: Through Frau Albrecht, his strict Volkshochschule Neukölln teacher, Jonas can point you to a class that corrects hard and kindly.
catchers.confirm: Are you in Berlin and preparing for roughly B1-level German?

catchers.hypo: I'm a freelancer in Berlin who has gone through delayed Ausländerbehörde appointments and permit extensions. I'd like to share what worked.
catchers.can: Jonas could really use practical advice or a referral to an immigration adviser, and could offer game-dev help or English proofreading in return.
catchers.confirm: Have you personally dealt with a self-employed residence permit extension in Berlin, not a work or student visa?

catchers.hypo: I'm struggling with anxious, sleepless months and the grind of solo creative work. I'd like another person who understands.
catchers.can: Jonas can offer company and honest conversation as a fellow solo dev, and can go bouldering or just talk, though he is not a professional counsellor.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for peer company rather than professional or clinical support?

catchers.hypo: I'd like to use your Godot journal UI idea in my own game. Is the plugin available, and could we cooperate on it?
catchers.can: Jonas can share the plugin early, take feedback, and tidy it up with other users' needs in mind.
catchers.confirm: Are you using Godot 4 and need a sprite-sheet-driven UI, not a full inventory system?

forbids.text: No crunch. I tried it at my old studio and it broke me.
I won't take investment that demands a pivot to mobile free-to-play.
I'm based in Berlin and can't commit to travel outside the Schengen area for now.
I can't afford unpaid work that takes time away from the demo before the February Next Fest.
I won't share my permit or passport details, or my exact finances, with anyone.

projects.name: Slow Water
projects.text: A pixel-art fishing game on a lake that slowly drains over a season. The core loop and 40-minute vertical slice work. It still needs the second half of the lake, the weather system, save-file migration and about half the audio, with a demo targeted for the February Next Fest.
roles_needed: shader or VFX advisor who can say 'good enough'
demo and Next Fest marketing advisor

projects.name: Fishing journal tool
projects.text: A small Godot plugin that turns a sprite sheet into a flip-through journal UI. It works for me, a few Discord users want it, and the code needs cleaning up before release.

policy.t1: When there's a real sign of fit, I'll share my schedule, grant milestones, rough budget, and which parts of the game are unfinished.
policy.t2: Once there's trust and I know who you are, I'll talk about the permit and visa timing, my money runway and the personal stress.
policy.never: Exact bank balance, passport and permit numbers, and health details, including sleep and anxiety specifics.
